# Qi2 vs. Qi2.2 vs. MagSafe

**Qi2** is the Wireless Power Consortium's (WPC) magnetic wireless charging standard. It adds a ring of magnets that aligns the phone and charger and caps out at 15W. It's based on Apple's MagSafe technology, which Apple contributed to ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)).

**Qi2.2** (the Qi v2.2.1 spec, branded **Qi2 25W**) is the faster update, launched in July 2025. It has the same magnetic design but allows up to 25W, nearly 70% more power. The WPC says it can charge a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**MagSafe** is Apple's own branding and certification program. Apple certifies accessories to deliver 15W on most iPhones and up to 25W on iPhone 16 and later. Certified MagSafe chargers also include an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify the charger, plus a magnetometer to prevent compass interference ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)). Apple's current MagSafe Charger is also certified for Qi2 25W, so the two overlap.

## Things to watch for

- **25W needs a newer iPhone.** Apple lists 25W for the iPhone 16 Plus, 16 Pro Max, 17 series and 18 Pro models. The iPhone Air gets 20W, and the iPhone 16 and 16 Pro get 22.5W. The iPhone 17e and iPhone 15 and earlier top out at 15W ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)). The iPhone 16e has no wireless charging per The Verge, though Apple's support page says it charges via Qi.
- **You need the right adapter.** For 25W, Apple recommends a 30W or greater USB-C power adapter. The charger usually doesn't include one.
- **"MagSafe-compatible" is not certification.** These chargers are usually just 7.5W with a ring of magnets ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)). To verify a Qi2 or Qi2 25W claim, you can search the [WPC certified products database](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/).
- **Android support is thin.** The Pixel 10 supports Qi2 at 15W, and the Pixel 10 Pro XL supports Qi2.2 at 25W. Samsung's Galaxy S26 line is "Qi2 Ready" and needs a magnetic case ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).

## If you're shopping

- **Apple MagSafe Charger (2 m), $49:** certified for Qi2 25W and 15W MagSafe. [Buy at Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m?fnode=7120d2e211c5d2008372acfadfa9b649c5ec92879b07e2f040e38952fcd8be0794ade18a93d927b4c96c7a13cda2597927c0814a65dc0189e774b77c7fdb7e748fe7efe26c0c6c21f59929ac37012aa0ac916746c2f56a8e6448ccdb97e7d384&fs=s%3Dnewest%26fh%3D8e12f5%252B81eaf8). The 1 m version was listed at about $39 in Macworld's review.
- **Baseus PicoGo AM52 Qi2.2 power bank (10,000mAh):** The Verge found it the fastest wireless performer of the seven it tested, at about $60 to $70.
